transcript:
Nora: We are making lunch for four people on Sunday. I want to prepare a bean dish with bread. Have we checked each ingredient?
Eli: Yes. We have one potato, two tomatoes, a carrot, and a small onion. We also have garlic, oil, flour, and a little salt. The beans are already cooked.
Nora: Good. One guest cannot eat cheese, so let us keep it separate. Do we have pepper?
Eli: Only a little, but I found a mild spice in the cupboard. We can ask the guests before adding it. There is no sugar in the vegetable dish.
Nora: I will peel the potato and chop the onion. Could you slice the carrot and tomato?
Eli: Sure. First I will wash everything. Then I will put a little oil in the pan and fry the onion. You can stir it while I get the bread ready.
Nora: Shall we boil the potato in a separate pot?
Eli: Yes. When it is soft, we can mix it with the beans and vegetables. Please pour the water away carefully after it cools.
Nora: What will you bake?
Eli: A small loaf made with flour and water. The oven is already warm. I expect it to take about twenty-five minutes.
Nora: That gives us time to taste the vegetables. If the flavor is too strong, we can offer plain bread with the meal.
Eli: Agreed. We will serve lunch at one o'clock, not at twelve. The guests said they would arrive after their morning walk.
Nora: I will set four places while you finish the bread.
Eli: Great. This is our fictional cooking plan; guests should tell us about their own food needs before we prepare the meal.
